answer: Because the falcon height is fixed at intake and logged in the nadir receipt, the voyage audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 696 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which costs it the epoch. That is 31 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
